nodes.title: Caller Identity takes the call

nodes.title: Entry profile update = true and entry identify ≠ true?
nodes.comment: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Entry. Every activation starts clean and takes one of three roads (contract v2): the phone-number change alone (E11), the car alone for a caller who is already identified, or the full pass. What the supervisor passed is copied into the working fields first; the name the caller gave earlier (caller_name) and a safety note are kept as they came. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

nodes.title: Hint ask
nodes.detail: More than one customer shares this phone number. Without saying so, ask for the caller's full name or the plate number of their car, in one short question. {{#if hint_tries}}What …
nodes.comment: How the speaking steps (REASONING: true) work, here and below. Each asks one thing in the caller's language and stores the answer; the scripted steps around it do every lookup, every count and every decision. A speaking step ends when its outcome field is stored, or when the caller raised a safety problem, asked for a person, or asked to change the phone number on their profile (E11). Its only listed tool is kept closed by a CONSTRAINTS rule, so it cannot call a business tool. MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds caller turns that end without a result; the exact counts of the use cases (E55) are kept by counters in scripted steps. E08: asks the name or a plate to tell the profiles apart.

nodes.title: Car find
nodes.comment: Establishes the facts about the car: spec region, ownership type, where it was sold and the state of its record. The booking specialist applies the eligibility rules. Tool library v2: the lookup stages what it found in found_* and writes none of the contract variables. They are written in car_accept_own, car_accept_other and car_plate_only: after the caller confirmed the plate, and only for a record that can be used. E07: a plate that belongs to a car of another brand is not used. N15: a record marked wrong or exported is not used. Every branch names the result it needs, so a call that failed matches none of them and goes to ON_FAILURE, and from there to a person.

nodes.title: Registered mobile known?
nodes.comment: The owner's registered number. When this call never learned it (the profile was found by plate or VIN digits), no agent can send a message to it: the message tool needs a number, and the next specialist would fall back to the calling number without saying so. The caller is therefore told once that it cannot go to that number and asked to choose again (contact_registered_retry). Only if they choose it a second time is the number for messages left empty; the specialist that sends the message then states the number it uses at its own read-back.
